liebermann.notes: The original of the London collection Leges Anglorum (c. 1210), which survives in copies; Liebermann’s Lond is the reading where K, Co, Or, Gi, Sl, Tw (or at least the first three) agree. Gi, Sl and Tw are known only from variants cited by 17th/18th-century editors. It contained the Expositio vocabulorum and Numerus provinciarum, then texts from the Quadripartitus with interpolated historical connections and supposed laws of London invention (incl. Pseudo-Ine, Pseudo-Alfred), then from the Tripartita the rubric list, Wl art retr, ECf retr with London interpolations and the Genealogia Normannica, and finally Henry I’s laws with his coronation charter and London charter.

entries.text_de:
nenne ich das verlorene Original der Leges Anglorum Londoniis s. XIII. in. collectae4 um 1210, dessen Lesart vorliegt, wo K Co Or Gi Sl Tw oder doch die drei ersten übereinstimmen. Von Gi Sl Tw kennen wir nur die Varianten, welche den Editoren des 17./18. Jhs. anzuführen gut schien. Wo ich Lond hinter Varianten setze, findet sich die Lesart in K Co Or.

Lond enthielt Expositio vocabulorum; Numerus provinciarum, hidarum5; dann aus Quadr. mit eingefügten historischen Verbindungen und angeblichen Gesetzen Londoner Erfindung: Ine, u. S. 89; Blas, Forf, u. S. 389; Hu, u. S. 192; Pseudo-Ine6; Af von Einl. 49, 9 ab, u. S. 47; AGu, u. S. 127; App. AGu, u. S. 394; EGu, u. S. 129; Pseudo-Af7; I As, As Alm, II As, u. S. 147 f. 151; Episc, u. S. 477; Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, u. S. 459—65; IV. V. III. VI As, u. S. 171. 167. 170. 173; Ordal, u. S. 386; Cn, u. S. 279.

Aus der Tripartita: Rubrikenliste8 zu Wl art retr und ECf retr, u. S. 670; Wl art retr, u. S. 489; ECf retr Lond interpol., u. S. 627; Geneal. Normannica9.

Alsdann Hn, u. S. 547 mit CHn cor (vgl. u. West) und Hn Lond, u. S. 521. 524.
entries.text_en:
is what I call the lost original of the Leges Anglorum Londoniis s. XIII. in. collectae4, c. 1210, whose reading is before us where K Co Or Gi Sl Tw, or at least the first three, agree. Of Gi Sl Tw we know only the variants which the editors of the 17th/18th centuries saw fit to cite. Where I put Lond after variants, the reading is found in K Co Or.

Lond contained Expositio vocabulorum; Numerus provinciarum, hidarum5; then from Quadr., with inserted historical links and supposed laws of London invention: Ine, below, p. 89; Blas, Forf, below, p. 389; Hu, below, p. 192; Pseudo-Ine6; Af from Introd. 49, 9 onwards, below, p. 47; AGu, below, p. 127; App. AGu, below, p. 394; EGu, below, p. 129; Pseudo-Af7; I As, As Alm, II As, below, pp. 147 f. 151; Episc, below, p. 477; Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, below, pp. 459—65; IV. V. III. VI As, below, pp. 171. 167. 170. 173; Ordal, below, p. 386; Cn, below, p. 279.

From the Tripartita: list of rubrics8 to Wl art retr and ECf retr, below, p. 670; Wl art retr, below, p. 489; ECf retr Lond interpol., below, p. 627; Geneal. Normannica9.

Then Hn, below, p. 547, with CHn cor (cf. below, West) and Hn Lond, below, pp. 521. 524.

transcription.doubts: The heading runs on into the text ('Lond nenne ich …' = 'Lond is what I call …'). Entry runs from col. 1 into col. 2 of p. xxxiv. In 'Rubrikenliste zu Wl art retr und ECf retr' the sigla are roman, not bold.

wormald.shelfmark: Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae ('London collection'; original lost, copies Rs, K2, Co, Or)
wormald.wormald_date: Reign of John (p. 238); Liebermann's early-13th-century date upheld by discovery of Rs (p. 237 n. 303)
wormald.wormald_origin: London; belongs to the history of John's reign (p. 238); its surviving copies were kept at or given to the Guildhall (pp. 237–8).
wormald.laws: Geographical; Ine, Blas, Forf, Hu; Historical; Af, AGu, App. AGu, EGu; Historical; I–II As, Episc, Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, III–VI As, Ordal; Historical; I–II Cn; Historical; Part II: Wl art, ECf, Geneal. Duc. Norm., Historical, CHn cor, Hn Lond, Hn, etc. (Table 4.7, pp. 240–1)
wormald.laws_liebermann: Quadr, Ine, Blas, Forf, Hu, Af, AGu, App AGu, EGu, I As, As Alm, II As, Episc, Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, IV As, V As, III As, VI As, Ordal, Cn, Wl art retr, ECf retr, Lond ECf, Hn, CHn cor, Hn Lond
wormald.other_contents: Large assemblage from Ine to Henry II, in chronological order with historical commentary; constitutional defensiveness and imperial assertion (p. 238).
wormald.overview: An early-thirteenth-century London compilation of English law from Ine to Henry II, which took its pre-twelfth-century texts from Quadripartitus, rearranged them chronologically (so Ine precedes Alfred) and added historical commentary. Although surviving only in later copies, it drew on the earliest stage of Quadripartitus.
wormald.key_quote: a large assemblage of legal texts from Ine to Henry II, drawing on Quadripartitus for the pre-twelfth-century period (p. 238)
wormald.doubts: A text, not a manuscript; included because Wormald treats its Quadripartitus as the earliest recension.
